Sources

Educational only, not medical advice. Schematic, not to scale; one cell stands for the tumour. Levels come from a qualitative model, not measurements. On a phone, tap a part for its explanation.

  • KRAS in PDA. Activating KRAS mutations in 90-95% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: Robbins & Kumar Basic Pathology 9th ed., ch. 19 (printed pp. 892-893, via the project's page-referenced facts in docs/book-notes/atlas-facts.json). Oncogenic Kras alone sufficient to initiate PanIN in mice: Kleeff J et al., Pancreatic cancer, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2016;2:16022, doi:10.1038/nrdp.2016.22 (PMID 27158978).
  • The RAS switch and G12 mutants. Simanshu DK, Nissley DV, McCormick F, Cell 2017;170:17-33, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2017.06.009 (PMID 28666118); Hobbs GA, Der CJ, Rossman KL, J Cell Sci 2016;129:1287-92, doi:10.1242/jcs.182873 (PMID 26985062).
  • Downstream arms. Cox AD et al., Nat Rev Drug Discov 2014;13:828-51, doi:10.1038/nrd4389 (PMID 25323927).
  • Alleles. G12D, G12V and G12R are the common PDA alleles; no percentages are shown because none was checked against a primary table.

Simplified. Receptors, growth-factor ligands, adaptors and the GEF (SOS) are not drawn; RAL, a third effector, is not drawn; each downstream arm is one box; protein shapes are cartoons. A mutant KRAS still cycles somewhat and its intrinsic GTPase is impaired (to a different degree by allele), so "stuck on" means mostly on. Left out: isoforms, other GEFs and GAPs, feedback, drug targeting, and other PDA genes (CDKN2A, TP53, SMAD4).
